Transformer, une terre jusqu'alors boisée, ou en friche, en terre cultivée : la rendre cultivable.

examples.text: Défrichez cette terre sauvage!
Au lieu de broussailles, des haies vives entouraient un enclos récemment défriché.

Une grande partie des bois qui couvraient le sol du département ont été défrichés, et cette pratique a été évidemment favorable à l'agriculture, car elle lui a livré des terres qui n'étaient auparavant que d'un très-faible rapport.

Nous ne faisons que traverser Loqueffret, bourg chétif, mais industrieux, comme tous ceux de cette région, où chacun défriche', ensemence son arpent de landes, et exerce par surcroît une foule de petits métiers.
Le royaume de Dieu est un champ qu'il faut défricher.

glosses: Défricher un domaine jusqu'alors inconnu: jeter les bases d'une science nouvelle.

examples.text: Champollion a défriché l'égyptologie.

[Sigmund Freud] À ses yeux, sa démarche n’est donc pas antagoniste de celle des neurosciences, bien au contraire, mais elle constitue une sorte d’éclaireur avancé qui défriche un terrain sur lequel les disciplines fondamentales pourront le jour venu s’engager. — (Lionel Naccache, Le Nouvel Inconscient : Freud, le Christophe Colomb des neurosciences, Odile Jacob, 2009, page 418)

glosses: Without clouds.

examples.text: clear weather; a clear day

examples.text: with a countenance as clear / As friendship wears at feasts

glosses: Easily or distinctly heard; audible.

glosses: Unmixed; entirely pure.

examples.text: clear sand

glosses: Without defects or blemishes, such as freckles or knots.

glosses: Good, the best.

examples.text: Nando's is clear.

glosses: Better than, superior to.

examples.text: Spurs are clear of Arsenal.

glosses: All the way; entirely.

examples.text: I threw it clear across the river to the other side.

glosses: Not near something or touching it.

examples.text: Stand clear of the rails, a train is coming.

glosses: Free (or separate) from others.

examples.text: Much soul-searching is going on at the west London club who, just seven weeks ago, were five points clear at the top of the table and playing with the verve with which they won the title last season.

glosses: In a clear manner; plainly.

examples.text:

glosses: To remove obstructions, impediments or other unwanted items from.

examples.text: Police took two hours to clear the road.
If you clear the table, I'll wash up.

Since the mid-1980s, when Indonesia first began to clear its bountiful forests on an industrial scale in favour of lucrative palm-oil plantations, “haze” has become an almost annual occurrence in South-East Asia. glosses: To remove (items or material) so as to leave something unobstructed or open.

examples.text: […] Aristotle has brought to explain his Doctrine of Substantial Forms, when he tells us that a Statue lies hid in a Block of Marble; and that the Art of the statuary only clears away the superfluous Matter, and removes the Rubbish.
Please clear all this stuff off the table.
The loggers came and cleared the trees.

glosses: To leave abruptly; to clear off or clear out.

examples.text: Then the whole population cleared into the forest, expecting all kinds of calamities to happen, while, on the other hand, the steamer Fresleven commanded left also in a bad panic, in charge of the engineer, I believe.

glosses: To become free from obstruction or obscurement; to become transparent.

examples.text: When the road cleared we continued our journey.
After a heavy rain, the sky cleared nicely for the evening.
Shake the test tube well, and the liquid should slowly clear.

glosses: To eliminate ambiguity or doubt from (a matter); to clarify or resolve; to clear up.

examples.text: We need to clear this issue once and for all.

glosses: To remove from suspicion, especially of having committed a crime.

examples.text: The court cleared the man of murder.
[…] yet I appeal to the reader, and am sure he will clear me from Partiality.
How! Wouldst thou clear rebellion?

glosses: To pass without interference; to miss.

examples.text: The door just barely clears the table as it closes.
The leaping horse easily cleared the hurdles.

glosses: To exceed a stated mark.

examples.text: She was the first female high jumper to clear two metres.

glosses: To finish or complete (a stage, challenge, or game).

examples.text: I cleared the first level in 36 seconds.

glosses: Of a check or financial transaction, to go through as payment; to be processed so that the money is transferred.

examples.text: The check might not clear for a couple of days.

glosses: To earn a profit of; to net.

examples.text: He's been clearing seven thousand a week.
The profit which she cleared on the cargo […] cannot be estimated at less than a thousand guineas.

glosses: To approve or authorise for a particular purpose or action; to give clearance to.

examples.text: Air traffic control cleared the plane to land.
The marketing department has cleared the press release for publication.

glosses: To obtain approval or authorisation in respect of.

examples.text: I've cleared the press release with the marketing department, so go ahead and publish it.

glosses: To obtain a clearance.

examples.text: The steamer cleared for Liverpool today.

glosses: To obtain permission to use (a sample of copyrighted audio) in another track.
To disengage oneself from incumbrances, distress, or entanglements; to become free.

examples.text: Beſides, he that cleares at once will relapſe: for finding himſelfe out of ſtraights, he will reuert to his cuſtomes. But hee that cleareth by degrees, induceth an habite of frugality, and gaineth as well vpon his minde, as vpon his Eſtate.

glosses: To hit, kick, head, punch etc. (a ball, puck) away in order to defend one's goal.

examples.text: The goalkeeper rushed forward to clear the ball.
A low cross came in, and Smith cleared.
Bolton then went even closer when Elmander's cross was met by a bullet header from Holden, which forced a wonderful tip over from Cech before Drogba then cleared the resulting corner off the line.

glosses: To reset or unset; to return to an empty state or to zero.

examples.text: to clear an array;  to clear a single bit (binary digit) in a value

glosses: To style (an element within a document) so that it is not permitted to float at a given position.

examples.text: To get the footer acting right, you need to float it and clear it on both margins.

glosses: To unload a firearm, or undergo an unloading procedure, in order to prevent negligent discharge; for safety reasons, to check whether one's firearm is loaded or unloaded.

examples.text: To prevent any shooting accidents, remember to clear your pistol and stay aware of your surroundings.

glosses: Full extent; distance between extreme limits; especially; the distance between the nearest surfaces of two bodies, or the space between walls.

examples.text: a room ten feet square in the clear

glosses: The completion of a stage or challenge, or of the whole game.

examples.text: It took me weeks to achieve a one-credit clear (1CC).

glosses: A person who is free from the influence of engrams.
